title: Volume 1 Chapter 4: Because We're Going to Support You for Life! 3
content:
Ijuuin didn’t answer.  
No, it’s more accurate to say she couldn’t answer.  
Her very identity was being denied by her own past actions.  
That was something no one else could be blamed for. I had no intention of letting her make excuses.  
Even if she tried, I would confront her with that contradiction.  
No matter how much she struggled, in the end, Ijuuin had no choice but to accept it.
So just admit it, Ijuuin.

The foolishness of what you tried to do. How rash your actions were.  
If you understand that, you can move forward.
“—I’m sorry, Ijuuin.”
[img]https://i.imgur.com/yhNHKBF.jpeg
For that reason, I decided to lend her a little help.
“I went a bit too far. It probably seemed like I was blaming you in front of everyone. That wasn’t my intention.”
I said, bowing my head.

“I asked something hard to answer. You even went so far as to transfer schools for their sake. Your passion for Damenzu is genuine, and I’m really sorry for saying things that made you doubt that. I honestly apologize, Ijuuin.”
“N-no, it’s nothing like that.”
“So—”
Seeing Ijuuin show a slight sense of relief, I smiled gently and said,
“I’ll accept this one hundred million yen, Ijuuin.”
She said it as if giving up.
“To be honest… I’m scared of going against a huge organization like the Ijuuin Conglomerate. I’m just an ordinary citizen, and I have no power or means to oppose you…”
She lowered her eyes and muttered self-deprecatingly.

Ijuuin didn’t seem to understand what I meant, but that was fine.  
From here on, willingly or not, she would come to understand. No, I would make her understand.

“This one hundred million was your mercy, right? You’re giving me severance pay to quietly back off, that’s what it means, isn’t it? If not… well, maybe I don’t need to say it. I get it. I’ll obey you. If I do, you won’t do anything. That’s how it is, right?”
“N-no, that’s not it at all! I would never—!”
“It’s fine. I understand. I don’t intend to oppose you. So I’ll take this money and quietly back off. Honestly, it’s really frustrating, though.”

Ijuuin understood the implication behind my words and tried to deny it, but it was already too late.  
The gazes around us were starting to include sympathy for me.
“But promise me one thing.”
Feeling that, I continued.
“Please take good care of them. I did accept the money, but those two were truly important to me.”
“And also, I’ll accept being separated from them… but surely you need to explain yourself, right? So sorry, but I’m going to say why.”
I opened my eyes wide at Ijuuin, then deliberately gave her a resigned smile.

“You told them they had to leave me because you said so. That you gave me one hundred million to make me leave. And that you put a fifty million yen value on each of them. You have to say that too, right?”
“Eh, ah…!”
“Can’t be helped, right? If you don’t, they won’t accept it. An explanation is necessary no matter what. What they think of you afterward is none of my business. But…”
I paused.
“If I were forcibly torn away from my childhood friends at that price, knowing I had to obey that person from now on… I’d never forgive them.”
Suppressing the grin that wanted to spread across my face, I said.
“Oh, and I forgot to mention, they didn’t become idols to support me. They became idols to support me. Do you understand what that means?”
“Mean…?”
“If I’m torn away from them, they might lose their reason to continue as idols. Maybe their motivation would just drop, but at worst, they might retire.”
I casually hinted at the worst possible future, mixing in information Ijuuin didn’t know.
“T-that’s…!”
“Wait! What have you done, Ijuuin!?”
Ijuuin was speechless, but in contrast, the classroom erupted in a sudden uproar at the word “retirement.”

“Well, show some pride as a single-digit fan club member and somehow convince them to keep singing for the fans… though, come to think of it, that reason might be taken away by the fans. But it can’t be helped. You decided to do this, so I can’t oppose that choice.”

I spoke as if it were someone else’s problem, but no one here was going to blame me anymore.  
There were many fans of Damenzu in this class, after all. All hostility was directed at Ijuuin.
“Convincing them is your job now. Good luck, Ijuuin. Once you take this money, it’s no longer my concern.”
Saying that, I reached for the attache case.
—Now, what will you do, Ijuuin? This is your last chance.

There was no written contract or record, but everyone in the classroom would surely testify to the exchange as fact.  
From the classmates’ perspective, it probably seemed less like severance pay to make me cut ties with Damenzu and more like Ijuuin forcibly bribing me to buy Damenzu. But that was unavoidable.

“Ijuuin-san, what are you going to do with Setsuna and Arisa!?”  
“Are you planning to destroy our Damenzu!?”  
“If that happens, we’ll never forgive you!”

Being cornered and blamed by classmates like this was inevitable.  
There was no contract, and the deal was made under the watchful eyes of the whole class.

Ijuuin must have underestimated me, but this was her own fault.  
All I did was manipulate impressions a little to increase the hate toward her.  
But that was caused by Ijuuin’s own weak moves in the first place.
(In short, you’re already cornered, Ijuuin.)

That’s why she ended up trapped like this. In the end, the world is made so that the one who gets deceived is at fault.  
If you don’t notice, it’s your fault. And even if you do, it’s too late to do anything. The situation was already set here.
“Now for the final touch.”

The moment Ijuuin accepted this one hundred million, it would be the final blow.  
I would become the victim forced to accept severance pay.  
Ijuuin would become the perpetrator who bought Damenzu with money and caused the breakup by tearing my childhood friends away.

From there, it would be a free fall.  
No excuses, Ijuuin would become the target of blame.  
The wealthy heiress who destroyed her beloved Dimension Stars! with her own hands.

Ijuuin wouldn’t be able to bear that.  
She transferred schools just to be close to Damenzu.  
It was impossible. She couldn’t do such a thing.
(Checkmate, Ijuuin.)

Slowly, deliberately, I reached out my hand.  
Once the contract was made, Ijuuin would be finished.

So what will you do? Ijuuin has no choice left.  
Yes, there is only one thing she can do.

To overturn this situation, she must cancel the original contract.  
So move, Ijuuin.  
You’re running out of time. Is that really what you want? It can’t be, right?  
Because Dimension Stars! are the goddesses of fate to you.

My fingers were just a few centimeters from the attache case.  
No time to think or hesitate.

Three centimeters. Two centimeters. One centimeter.  
Ah, almost there.

It felt like time was stretched infinitely.  
This moment would surely be a turning point in my life.  
And the same for Ijuuin.  
Our turning points overlapped—and then it came.
“——Hnnngh!!!!”

The moment I heard the shout, my right hand reaching for the attache case swung and missed.  
A whooshing sound of something being thrown reached my ears a moment later.

There was Ijuuin, arms raised high in front of the desk, and above her, a black attache case and bundles of bills were flying through the air.  
Some of the bundles had their bands come undone, scattering millions of yen notes like confetti.
My eyes caught the surreal moment as if watching slow-motion footage.
And I thought—
—I’ve won, Ijuuin.

Thud!  
As my senses caught up to reality, I heard a heavy object fall.

I caught a glimpse out of the corner of my eye of Gotou-kun, who had taken the falling attache case on his head, and Yuki-chan, who was hit by the flying bills as if sucked in.  
But they seemed fine, so that was good.

What mattered to me was the young lady in front of me.  
While shoving some of the recovered million-yen bundles into the desk, I asked the panting Ijuuin who had thrown the attache case,
“Hah, hah… what’s the meaning of this, Ijuuin? I was going to accept the one hundred million yen. What’s going on?”
“Th-that is invalid, invalid. I was wrong….”
“Wrong? What do you mean? I don’t think your actions were wrong.”
I said feigning ignorance. Ijuuin, regretting her mistake, didn’t notice.
“It was all a mistake… trying to forcibly tear those two away from you. Putting a price on Dimension Stars!… all of it was my mistake.”
“Oh? Then what will you do? You can’t undo the past. It’s true you tried to bribe them.”
“I know. I know…! If mistakes can’t be undone…!”
Her determined eyes caught mine.
“Could you please explain to them what happened here?”
“Explain? Why would I do that?”
“If I don’t admit my guilt, I can’t move forward… I can’t walk the path of resolve to live for Damenzu!”
“Resolve? To you, those two are only worth one hundred million yen, so you have no resolve.”
“No. Those two can never be given a price! I won’t make that mistake again… I will devote my money, time, and even my life to Dimension Stars!! That is my resolve!!!”

Hearing that, I struggled to keep my mouth from loosening.  
I already understood perfectly what she was going to say next.
“Hmph… but words are easy to say.”
“Yes. So please let me prove it. Let me prove I will live for Dimension Stars!”
“Prove it?”
She closed her eyes quietly once and said,
“…I will support them.”
“Huh? What did you say?”
“I will support you for life in their place!!!”

She declared it with strength.  
Hearing those words, I finally smiled.
“Ijuuin…”

Yes, that’s right.  
That’s good, Ijuuin.
“That’s your resolve. Then…”
I wanted to hear those words.
“I’ll accept it, Ijuuin. If you’re going to support me, I can’t refuse.”

Saying you don’t want to work is easy.  
Actually not working depends on your will, if you don’t care about others’ eyes or social norms.

Many say foolish things like “buy your hardships when young” or “working is natural,” which don’t fit the times.  
If you have enough money to live without working for life, few would choose to work.

No matter how much you put on a show, people can’t resist temptation.  
Wanting to escape to ease rather than endure pain is normal human thinking.

Yet most people start working when they enter society.  
Why? The answer is simple: money.

Even if you have enough savings to live alone, once you marry and have children, you have to keep working.  
Society uses the responsibility born from becoming a parent as lubricant to make you work.

With family held hostage, you must work, becoming a cog in the company, used up as labor.  
Children grow up watching their parents, imprinting that working is natural.

The result is obvious.  
Though the paths differ, they end the same as their parents.  
A never-ending cycle of exploitation.

It’s built into the system of our world, impossible to escape.  
Even if you don’t accept it, people get used to it. They’re also easily swayed.

It’s easier to go with the flow than to resist.  
They keep following those who exploit them, complaining but never leaving the system.

So the people above keep getting richer, and those below keep working.  
The invisible, unfair line remains, and the cycle spins endlessly.

Now, back to the point.  
What I want to say is that if you don’t want to work, you need the effort and resolve to match.

Even if you have two childhood friends as idols and an environment where you get pocket money and are supported, I wasn’t satisfied.  
Because I absolutely don’t want to work. Absolutely, absolutely, absolutely.
People who say they don’t want to work but don’t build an environment to avoid it and then complain when they have to work have a completely different resolve.

Idol work can earn big money while still students, but it’s a popularity business.  
Popularity is fickle; even if things are good now, there are many pitfalls ahead.

Damenzu’s popularity might suddenly plummet, and they might stop earning.  
Or they might get injured and be unable to perform.  
Or illness.  
Or agency scandals.  
Etcetera, etcetera.
The list is endless. If that happens, I won’t be supported.
Some might say, “You’ve been supported so now you should work,” or “Stick with them and support them,” but that’s nonsense.

To avoid that, I always keep an eye on them.  
I check their live shows and such. But misfortune can strike suddenly.

Good now doesn’t guarantee the future.  
It’s easy to look away from “what if,” but that’s just avoidance. Reality is always merciless.  
That’s why you have to prepare.
For yourself and for them, it’s natural to seek ways to raise the probability of absolute success.

Not wanting to work and wanting to take it easy are different.  
Those who forget trial and error and just run to ease, stopping thought there, have no right to say they don’t want to work.

At least, I don’t accept such people.  
I’m different from scum who just parasitize others and blindly think only of a happy future.

I used to deny gambling for a big win, but entrusting your life to others is also a kind of gamble.  
That’s why the more people and money supporting you, the better.  
That closes holes and makes absolutes more certain.

This case was part of that.  
Setsuna and the others, who started climbing the ladder as popular idols, and Ijuuin, born into a conglomerate that can move hundreds of millions overnight, live on completely different stages.

Idol <<<< (an unbreakable wall) <<<< Conglomerate Heiress  
That’s an absolute equation.
The stability is different, and the connections and influence available are on a different level.
It would have been easy to just get more money, but that would sever relations, and Ijuuin’s impression of me would remain bad.
“For the record, Ijuuin, no second thoughts, right? This time you can’t take it back.”

That’s why I shook Ijuuin and cornered her, forcing her to act.  
Getting her to promise to support me was the plan I pictured the moment I saw the one hundred million yen attache case.
“Of course, I swear on the name of the Ijuuin Conglomerate.”
“By the way, does that contract imply you’ll stop taking money from those two?”
“I’ll leave that to you. But… I guarantee you can live a life of leisure without receiving money from anyone.”
That was basically a yes, but I didn’t press it.
“Really? You’ll feed me high-end sushi and A5 meat every day? I’ll pull gacha as much as I want, spam super chats, and get luxury apartments all over Japan?”
“That’s fine. A5, bluefin tuna, a thousand gacha pulls, the highest royal suite hotel, luxury condos—eat, sleep, buy, and use as much as you want. Whatever you do, I’m ready to accept it all.”

Ijuuin’s eyes looked straight at me without hesitation.  
She had made up her mind. She would surely carry this will for life.  
Even if society thinks she’s on the wrong path.
“…Those eyes. They don’t lie.”
“Yes. Everything is for Dimension Stars! I’m here for that alone.”

Ijuuin was resolved to go down with Dimension Stars!  
Even if Ichinose warned her, she wouldn’t accept it.
“No more hesitation, huh? You look great, Ijuuin. With that, you could probably join Dimension Stars! and be an idol, right?”
“Hmph, don’t be ridiculous. I could never stand alongside them… but I’ll gratefully accept that compliment, even if it’s flattery.”
“It’s not flattery. I really think you’re a beauty everyone admires, Ijuuin. Hold your head high. I guarantee it.”
“…You’re really terrible, Kazuma-sama. If not for this encounter, I probably would have…”

Blushing and fiddling with her wavy hair, Ijuuin showed no trace of the proud heiress she once was.  
Seeing her growth with a smile, I was inwardly certain of my victory.
The plan was reaching its moment of fulfillment. Only the final touch remained.
“I understand your resolve. Then I must respond.”
“Ah…”
“I’ll tell them about your resolve, Ijuuin. You said it was a sin, but your feelings for Dimension Stars! are definitely real. If you talk properly, they’ll surely understand.”
I answered with a wry smile, and tears welled up in Ijuuin’s eyes.
“Th-thank you!”
“Just don’t forget—if you break the contract, I’ll immediately parasitize Setsuna and Arisa again and leech money, okay? Keep that in mind.”

Saying that, I reached out my right hand to Ijuuin.  
To seal the contract with a handshake.
Noticing my intention, Ijuuin also extended her hand toward me.
“Yes. Then…”
“Contract established.”
We were supposed to shake firmly, but—

“Good morning, everyone!”  
“Morning. Hey, what are you all doing…?”
With a loud noise and dazzling sparkle, they appeared.
“Setsuna, Arisa. You just got here…”

I knew they would come, but what terrible timing… or maybe, on second thought, it was good?  
I was going to talk anyway, so riding this flow was fine.
As I thought that, they approached me.
“Wow, yen bills are flying around. Like confetti.”
“You don’t see this even in dramas… This has to be your doing, right? Explain what happened, Kazuma.”

Setsuna was curiously watching the fluttering bills, but Arisa assumed I was involved from the start.  
Well, she wasn’t wrong. But still, I wish they trusted me more.
My daily behavior might not be great, but the trigger was Ijuuin, not me.
Thinking that, I briefly explained to the two who had just arrived and didn’t grasp the situation.

“Well, a lot happened. I’ll explain the details later, but the problem was just solved, and you showed up just as we were wrapping up. They say the star arrives late, but coming right before the curtain call is unfortunate.”
“I want to know what that ‘lot’ is…”
“Well, it’s fine, Arisa. If Kazu-kun says it’s solved, that’s good enough.”

Setsuna supported Arisa, who was about to dig deeper.  
I appreciated that kindness. Setsuna’s sweetness toward me was one of her best traits.
“Setsuna’s always like that… Sigh, if the talk’s over, then fine, but shouldn’t we sit down? Homeroom is almost over.”
“Oh! Right! Sensei, I want to get back to the staff room soon to prepare for class, so everyone sit down…”
“Wait. Before that, I have something to say to you two.”
“Say what?”
“Again? Enough already! Hurry up or the head teacher will scold me again! Please let homeroom proceed!”

Ignoring the nearly crying Yuki-chan, I looked straight at my childhood friends.  
This was a precious opportunity. I couldn’t waste this timing.

Homeroom happens every morning, but doing something only possible now is more important for students.  
I hoped the teacher would consider that.  
This experience would surely be valuable for Yuki-chan, and it wasn’t a bad thing.  
Though I didn’t know where it would be useful.
“Actually, I have something important to tell you two.”
“What is it? Oh, is it that we’re out of money?”
“Kazuma, you’re hopeless. How much do we have now…”
“No, that’s not it. It’s not about pocket money. What I want to talk about is something else.”

I stopped them from pulling out their wallets.  
Sure, they wanted pocket money, but that wasn’t the priority now.
“Then what?”
“Well… actually…”
“Don’t beat around the bush. Just say it. It’s probably nothing important anyway, right?”

Arisa looked at me suspiciously.  
Her sharp attitude hadn’t changed since childhood, and I couldn’t help but smile wryly.
“Maybe so. But just listen quietly. This is pretty important.”
